b: GM Hikaru Nakamura, one of the game's leading players and most influential content creators, has renewed with Chess.com, extending a longstanding partnership.

From record-breaking blitz performances to introducing chess to new audiences through streaming and PogChamps, the 38-year-old world number-two has made both competing and creating content part of one incredible chess career.
Hikaru has now signed a new long-term agreement with Chess.com, extending a partnership that began in 2013.

The new chapter in his Chess.com career gets a jump-start with the upcoming Salesforce FIDE World Championship 2026, where Hikaru will join the Chess.com commentary team for some key games and comment on the rest of the games on his Kick channel. Fans can also look forward to an exciting Hikaru vs. The World match, set to take place in 2027.
Hikaru Nakamura playing Titled Tuesday during Chess.com's Meetup in Greece. Photo: Chess.com.

"It's been an incredible journey seeing Chess.com grow from a small company with no more than 50 employees to what it is today, and to see the dramatic rise of chess during my time with the company," Hikaru said.

"There have been so many memories and inflection points along the way: Danny, a small-time executive at the time, reaching out to try to convince me to stream; covering the 2018 World Championship with the monkey-clapping memes; the whole golden age of the chess boom in 2020 and 2021, with xQc, Reckful, and other streamers playing chess, culminating in PogChamps and blockbuster TV shows like The Queen's Gambit."
"The whole ride has been amazing to be a part of," he added.
The whole ride has been amazing to be a part of.
Chess.com Chief Chess Officer IM Danny Rensch also welcomed the renewed agreement.

"Hikaru has been with Chess.com through so many wild rides, from every edition of the Speed Chess Championship to the PRO Chess League, and PogChamps, to countless Titled Tuesdays and Bullet Brawls, and so, so much more," he said.

"As a player and creator, he has inspired generations and blazed a trail for those who will come after him. We are so excited to have been partnered with Hikaru for over a decade, and we are thrilled for this next chapter."
Hikaru Nakamura against Magnus Carlsen in Norway Chess 2024. Photo: Maria Emelianova/Chess.com.

With 8.6 million followers across his social media platforms, Hikaru has played a key role in bringing chess to new audiences and helping grow the game's popularity. As a coach and commentator in the first PogChamps, one of the most-watched chess events of all time, he helped make chess approachable for creators and viewers discovering the game together.

His streams, YouTube videos, and shorts have entertained millions, and shown how one of the world's top grandmasters could entertain, teach, and build a community. In doing so, he helped pave the way for the chess creator scene that followed.

One of PogChamps’ most memorable moments came during Hikaru and WFM Alexandra Botez’s commentary of the xQc vs. Moistcr1tikal match, which ended much sooner than either expected. The clip has been viewed more than 26 million times.
His streaming career has produced plenty of milestones, and some unusual personal bests:
Most new subscribers on a single day: 13,609 (January 8, 2021)
Most bullet games won in an hour: 52 (June 1, 2021)
Highest Bullet Brawl Score: 320 arena points

While growing his online streaming and creator career, Hikaru continued to prove himself at the highest level over the board. His achievements include five U.S. Championship titles, victory in the 2011 Tata Steel Chess Masters, 2022 Fischer Random World Championship, the 2023 Norway Chess title, and his bayou-based detour in the 2025 Louisiana State Championship, which paved his road to the Candidates the following year.

This year, Hikaru made his fourth appearance at the FIDE Candidates Tournament, once again competing for a shot at the world championship, while bringing fans along through his YouTube recaps. The videos offered a firsthand account of his games and thought process, combining top-level events with the content creation that has become central to his career.

On Chess.com, his remarkable record spans the platform's biggest championships and its weekly tournaments. He won five consecutive Speed Chess Championships from 2018 through 2022, and has four Bullet Chess Championship titles, including a 17-15 victory over GM Magnus Carlsen in a thrilling 2023 final.

More recently, he pushed the Chess.com blitz rating record to 3503. He also leads Titled Tuesday with an astonishing 94 victories in the 11-round era, and Bullet Brawl's all-time winners list with 73 titles—more than twice the next-highest total.
Whether viewers first encountered him coaching a streamer, winning a Speed Chess final, or explaining a Candidates game, Hikaru has offered them a way into the sport.
With World Championship commentary and Hikaru vs. The World ahead, the renewed partnership will give fans more opportunities to learn from him—and a chance to play against him.
Alongside his appearances on Chess.com's commentary team, Hikaru will cover every day of the Salesforce FIDE World Championship on his Kick channel. Will you be watching?
